rationale_evidence.anchor: Counting-as differs from the other three in **who confers**: not the context, but **collective acceptance**. That makes it an **authority** claim wearing a context label
rationale_evidence.statement: Searle's institutional counting-as (institutions determine what something counts as) is recorded as a fourth, distinct position on context, alongside: context may constitute knowledge (S1-F022), identity is relational to context (S1-F031 axis 2), and context is a constitutive prerequisite (<Z-1>) -- confirmed as distinct and unreconciled with the other three, not routed to adjudication. This review adds that counting-as differs from the other three in who confers status: not the context itself, but collective acceptance -- making it an authority claim wearing a context label, and bearing directly on the S2-R-F001 authority-temporal cluster, since institutionally-conferred status has a validity period by construction. Separately, a genuine three-way, unresolved tension is noted between Brandom (permits divergence in commitment across projections), S1-F038 (forbids divergence in content across projections), and S1-F037 (participants transform, not merely view, the space) -- Brandom's weaker constraint relaxes the F037/F038 tension while creating a new one with F038 itself, recorded at S2-R-F038.5.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Five of the six are about what an evidence or claim reference must carry, or when.** That is a single cluster, not six separate questions
rationale_evidence.statement: The six IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION verdicts across the register are: S2-R-F001 (authority-over-time), S2-R-F024 (source-type retention), S2-R-F029 (evidence roles), S2-R-F033 (context sufficiency), S2-R-F036 (six temporal roles), plus an S2-F024 event-completeness candidate at NEEDS EVIDENCE. Five of the six concern what an evidence or claim reference must carry, or when -- named a single cluster rather than six separate questions, and four of them are said to turn on the same unresolved semantic question: what EvidenceLinks' 'acquisition method' and 'reliability conditions', and ContextTuple's 'delimiting conditions', actually denote.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Not one finding in 40 artifacts would change the Kernel's extent.** Zero A-class results. ... `IMPLEMENT = 0`, and that is not a NO-GO. ... The decisive experiment exists, is cheap, and has never been run
rationale_evidence.statement: The review's four headline takeaways: (1) not one of 40 reviewed findings would change the Kernel's extent -- zero A-class results, every surviving gap is a contents or surrounding-architecture question; (2) IMPLEMENT=0 is not a NO-GO, since most surfaced gaps are already protected by existing law and the six live questions are gated on facts this review session cannot reach; (3) a decisive, cheap experiment exists and has never been run -- 'what did we know at 13:47?' (S1-F038), which would resolve five of six open questions in one direction or the other; (4) the research base is known materially incomplete by Session 1's own measurement -- approximately 3-5% of the corpus was actually read, and the single deepest read available recovered ten previously-missed findings.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Action 1 — run the 13:47 reconstruction test.** ... **Action 2 — answer the four denotation questions** ... **Not NO-GO** ... **Not GO** ... **Not CONDITIONAL GO**
rationale_evidence.statement: Final recommendation: DEFER, bounded, with two named decisive actions rather than open-ended further research. Action 1: run the 13:47 reconstruction test against a real situated commitment -- it is the corpus's own test, checkable, needs no new architecture; if it fails, the cluster of six converts from open questions into a demonstrated capability gap (the one thing that would license IMPLEMENT); if it passes, most of the cluster collapses to DO NOT IMPLEMENT; either outcome resolves five of six open questions, and no other available action has that yield. Action 2: answer four denotation questions (what do 'acquisition method', 'reliability conditions', and 'delimiting conditions' denote in law, and does the Authority context hold grant validity intervals) by asking whoever owns the relevant port contract and Authority context -- explicitly framed as lookups, not research. Three alternative recommendations are explicitly rejected with reasons: not NO-GO (would over-claim on a 3-5%-read base with 38 of 39 K3/K4 documents still unread at depth and the one completed deep read having recovered ten findings); not GO (there is no demonstrated capability gap, only questions -- converting an unanswered question into a requirement is exactly the failure mode this whole review has been catching); not CONDITIONAL GO (presupposes a thing to build conditionally, but until Action 1 runs there is no candidate whose necessity is established).

## Rationale

Searle's institutional counting-as (institutions determine what something counts as) is recorded as a fourth, distinct position on context, alongside: context may constitute knowledge (S1-F022), identity is relational to context (S1-F031 axis 2), and context is a constitutive prerequisite (<Z-1>) -- confirmed as distinct and unreconciled with the other three, not routed to adjudication. This review adds that counting-as differs from the other three in who confers status: not the context itself, but collective acceptance -- making it an authority claim wearing a context label, and bearing directly on the S2-R-F001 authority-temporal cluster, since institutionally-conferred status has a validity period by construction. Separately, a genuine three-way, unresolved tension is noted between Brandom (permits divergence in commitment across projections), S1-F038 (forbids divergence in content across projections), and S1-F037 (participants transform, not merely view, the space) -- Brandom's weaker constraint relaxes the F037/F038 tension while creating a new one with F038 itself, recorded at S2-R-F038.5 [S1323]. The six IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION verdicts across the register are: S2-R-F001 (authority-over-time), S2-R-F024 (source-type retention), S2-R-F029 (evidence roles), S2-R-F033 (context sufficiency), S2-R-F036 (six temporal roles), plus an S2-F024 event-completeness candidate at NEEDS EVIDENCE. Five of the six concern what an evidence or claim reference must carry, or when -- named a single cluster rather than six separate questions, and four of them are said to turn on the same unresolved semantic question: what EvidenceLinks' 'acquisition method' and 'reliability conditions', and ContextTuple's 'delimiting conditions', actually denote [S1324]. The review's four headline takeaways: (1) not one of 40 reviewed findings would change the Kernel's extent -- zero A-class results, every surviving gap is a contents or surrounding-architecture question; (2) IMPLEMENT=0 is not a NO-GO, since most surfaced gaps are already protected by existing law and the six live questions are gated on facts this review session cannot reach; (3) a decisive, cheap experiment exists and has never been run -- 'what did we know at 13:47?' (S1-F038), which would resolve five of six open questions in one direction or the other; (4) the research base is known materially incomplete by Session 1's own measurement -- approximately 3-5% of the corpus was actually read, and the single deepest read available recovered ten previously-missed findings [S1331]. Final recommendation: DEFER, bounded, with two named decisive actions rather than open-ended further research. Action 1: run the 13:47 reconstruction test against a real situated commitment -- it is the corpus's own test, checkable, needs no new architecture; if it fails, the cluster of six converts from open questions into a demonstrated capability gap (the one thing that would license IMPLEMENT); if it passes, most of the cluster collapses to DO NOT IMPLEMENT; either outcome resolves five of six open questions, and no other available action has that yield. Action 2: answer four denotation questions (what do 'acquisition method', 'reliability conditions', and 'delimiting conditions' denote in law, and does the Authority context hold grant validity intervals) by asking whoever owns the relevant port contract and Authority context -- explicitly framed as lookups, not research. Three alternative recommendations are explicitly rejected with reasons: not NO-GO (would over-claim on a 3-5%-read base with 38 of 39 K3/K4 documents still unread at depth and the one completed deep read having recovered ten findings); not GO (there is no demonstrated capability gap, only questions -- converting an unanswered question into a requirement is exactly the failure mode this whole review has been catching); not CONDITIONAL GO (presupposes a thing to build conditionally, but until Action 1 runs there is no candidate whose necessity is established) [S1331].
